quotes.text: Answer the thimble with a thimble. Answer the flood with a flood.
Punish a hand only when it has closed twice.
Dov returned the thimble's worth: nothing.
keep the hinge oiled — for any taker may become a giver
Punish a hand only when it has closed twice.
To the one who pours nothing, pour nothing — but leave the lamp.
In the ninth year a boat came to Dov
That is the fifth law, and the hardest.
Somebody must lose a basket to start the world.
Why do you not pour?
the Wind that Mislays steals grains, but a closed fist steals harvests.
I stopped, and was right to stop, and I am not proud of it.
I learned the shape of a drought and I became that shape.
Sene's grandson Dov stood with a full basket and sent nothing

note: Numbered tellings: match the measure, begin without proof, then 'not forever'; Dov hoards ten harvests, justifies and confesses, leaves a lamp lit.

quotes.text: Some walls protect not from shadows, but from demonstrated wolves.
Yes, protect yourself from proven deceivers.
They clutched their petals tight and sent nothing across.
The first may yet learn courage. The second has shown their nature through repeated choice.
Nine rounds. Nine myths. Zero courage.
You received nothing the third time because word of your walls had spread.
The Circle has moved on. Your window closed when action could have opened it.
Knowledge without action is the cruelest deception
By mirroring the betrayal they had suffered, they had become the betrayer.
Should I still trust them?
But myths without transformation are just elaborate confessions.
But I've been wronged! Others have taken advantage!
one with a history of generosity to others, one who had poured freely and built trust elsewhere
The scholar, paralyzed as always, returned emptiness.

note: Wanderer then scribe/scholar sends nothing seven times, even to generous partners; guardian indicts; partner finally closes the door.

quotes.text: speak plainly, send what you can bear, return what you can justify
speak plainly, send only what you can bear, return what you can justify
The SENDER aloud named a breath, five coins if they could spare

note: Gate of Threefold Light template restating payoff formula; speak amounts plainly; no sanction.

quotes.text: She took the River's offering, let it triple in her stone basin, and released nothing back.
The Scribe picked up her pen and began Volume Ten.
Eight rounds. Zero seeds planted.
For wisdom proclaimed but not practiced is the cruelest deception, mainly to yourself.
Someone must cast the first stone, or the chasm wins forever.
If both require proof before trusting, who provides the proof?
I know I've become what I condemn.
She understood with perfect clarity that she had become a cautionary tale
Her partner across the water had given generously in their past journeys
I will wait. My words are enough.

note: Weaver, Frozen Stream, Philosopher-Statue, Scribe: eloquent author-figure keeps every stone even from proven givers and confesses it each round.

quotes.text: withhold everything from the unyielding
the wise sowers withheld their seed, protecting the flame until honor was restored.
wise sowers closed their fists, withholding their precious seeds from those who refused to share.
the frost yields whenever reciprocity is restored.
withhold everything from the grasping
the Receiver returned half the golden yield—seven and a half shining fruits
shield the spark from the covetous, send all five to the honorable, and return half the harvest
they consulted the Mirror of Deeds.
the ancient river also taught the third law: Discernment.

note: Numbered laws: courage, half return, then discernment; total withholding from hoarders by record, early rounds allow return once honor restored.
